tasks.short: Screen Recruitee applicants against the vacancy requirements (licences, certificates, shifts) and pass the suitable ones to the hiring manager.

today.trigger: New applications arrive in Recruitee, several times a week per open role, with peaks before the season when flex and fixed roles open together.
steps: Open each new candidate in Recruitee and read the CV and screening answers
Check hard requirements: driving licence C/CE, code 95, forklift or VCA certificate, shift availability, work permit
Move candidates to 'Shortlist' or 'Rejected' and add a note
Email or Teams the hiring manager with the shortlist and chase their feedback
drudgery: Reading the same CV fields again and again for licence and certificate checks
Chasing managers who do not open the shortlist
today.time_sinks: Reading badly structured CVs and Dutch/Polish/English mixed applications, and chasing manager feedback.

lenses.faster: An LLM step extracts licences, certificates, shift availability and language from each CV into Recruitee fields, so the administrator checks a table instead of reading CVs.
lenses.autonomous: On a new application, the extraction runs and the candidate card is filled; a stalled shortlist triggers a manager reminder after two days.
lenses.ambitious: Every applicant gets a response within 48 hours and every rejected-but-qualified candidate is matched to other open roles across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
lenses.joy: No more reading CVs for a licence code; the administrator spends time on phone screens with the borderline candidates.
lenses.options: Show the manager three ranked shortlists (strict on requirements, flexible on experience, internal and flex workers first) instead of one list.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the requirement checklist per role family and audits the extraction for errors and bias each month.
reach: Recruiter: first phone screens for warehouse and driver roles
L&D Specialist: flag candidates whose certificates expire soon so training can be planned

tasks.human_edge: Judging motivation, reliability and fit for shift work, and deciding who goes to the manager, stays with a person; AI-assisted applicant screening becomes high-risk under the EU AI Act from December 2027.
tasks.pattern_why: Requirement extraction is checkable, but selecting applicants is a decision about people that must not rest on the model alone (GDPR Art. 22, AI Act Annex III 4(a)).

in_practice.trigger: New candidate enters a Recruitee pipeline.
steps: Extract licences, certificates, availability and languages from CV and form into structured fields
Compare fields with the role's requirement checklist and mark met / not met / unclear
Administrator reviews the table, decides shortlist, writes a one-line note
Send shortlist to hiring manager in Teams with a two-day reminder
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator decides every shortlist and rejection; the model only fills fields and flags gaps.
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes and an extraction log kept for AI Act and works council review.

evidence.claim: Applicant screening and selection is high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(a) from 2 December 2027.
Decisions on applicants cannot rest solely on automated processing.
LLMs extract structured fields from CVs reliably enough for human review.

risks: Bias against non-standard CVs or non-native writers
Works council consent needed (WOR art. 27) for a tool processing applicant data
Administrator rubber-stamps the model's 'not met' flags
research_questions: What share of rejections today are on hard requirements versus judgement?
How accurate is extraction of licence and certificate data on 200 past Noordhaven CVs?
Does Recruitee allow custom fields to be written by an external service via its API?

tasks.short: Send applicants the rejection, invitation or offer email from Recruitee once a decision is made.

today.trigger: A recruiter or hiring manager decides on a candidate, or a candidate has waited too long.
steps: Find the decision in Recruitee notes, Teams or email
Pick a template and adjust it by hand for role and language
Send from Recruitee and move the candidate stage
Answer follow-up questions from rejected applicants
drudgery: Hunting for decisions in chat threads
Retyping the same rejection with small changes
today.time_sinks: Waiting for and finding the decision, not writing the message.

lenses.faster: A stage move in Recruitee sends the right template in the candidate's language automatically, with the reason fields filled.
lenses.autonomous: Rejection messages go out on a set delay after the stage change; candidates idle for 10 days get a status update without anyone remembering.
lenses.ambitious: Every rejected candidate gets a short, specific reason and a link to other open roles, which lifts the talent pool for peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing 'unfortunately' forty times a week; the administrator keeps the calls to finalists.
lenses.options: The LLM drafts three tones for a sensitive rejection (internal candidate, late-stage finalist) and the administrator picks one.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the template library and the trigger rules, and reviews candidate replies for tone problems.
reach: Recruiter: candidate status updates and post-rejection talent-pool follow-up

tasks.human_edge: Phoning finalists and internal candidates who were not chosen, and handling upset replies, stays personal.
tasks.pattern_why: Decision is made by a person in Recruitee; sending the right template on a stage change is a rule, with an optional LLM step only for personalised reasons.

in_practice.trigger: Candidate moved to Rejected, Interview or Offer stage in Recruitee.
steps: Recruitee automation picks template by stage, role family and language
Optional LLM step drafts a one-line personalised reason from the recruiter's note
Message waits in a delayed-send queue for 24 hours
Internal and late-stage candidates are routed to the administrator for a call instead
in_practice.human_gate: The stage change itself is the human decision; personalised reasons are approved before send.

evidence.claim: The acceptance or rejection letter can be automated as long as the decision is not solely automated.
ATS tools including Recruitee send templated emails on pipeline stage changes.

risks: Wrong stage click sends a rejection to the wrong candidate
Generated reasons that reveal discriminatory or unlawful grounds
research_questions: How many hours a week go to finding decisions versus writing messages?
How often are stages moved by mistake today?
Do candidates rate personalised rejections higher in the Recruitee survey?

tasks.short: Handle benefits (pension, bike plan, travel allowance) and sickness/WIA paperwork with UWV and the insurer in AFAS.

today.trigger: Employee question, new hire, contract change, long-term sickness milestone, or insurer/UWV letter.
steps: Look up the employee's contract, CAO scale and arrangement in AFAS
Answer the question or fill the pension fund, bike plan or UWV form
Process the mutation in AFAS for payroll
File the document in the digital dossier and track deadlines
drudgery: Answering the same travel allowance and pension questions
Rekeying letters from UWV, the pension fund and the insurer into AFAS
today.time_sinks: Repeated questions and manual intake of incoming letters.

lenses.faster: Incoming letters are read into dossier fields (AFAS Jonas style) and standard questions are answered from a lookup of the person's own entitlements.
lenses.autonomous: A contract change in AFAS triggers the pension and allowance mutations and a checklist; WIA and Poortwachter deadlines raise tasks without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Every employee, including night-shift warehouse staff, gets a clear personal overview of benefits in their own language.
lenses.joy: Gone: copying UWV letters into fields and repeating the reiskosten rule; left: helping someone through long-term sickness or a pension choice.
lenses.options: For a benefit change the bot shows two or three scenarios (e.g. part-time pension effect) from the deterministic calculation.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the benefits knowledge base and the exceptions queue, and checks a weekly sample of answers and mutations.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: first-line benefit questions
Payroll Specialist: pre-validated mutations before month close

tasks.human_edge: Sickness and incapacity cases involve health data and personal situations; conversations and judgement stay human.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across AFAS and external portals, with exceptions; entitlements are deterministic lookups, letters are LLM-read, and a person approves each mutation.

in_practice.trigger: Employee question in Teams, contract mutation in AFAS, or incoming letter.
steps: Classify the request and identify the employee
Quote entitlements from an AFAS lookup, never generated
Read incoming letters into proposed dossier fields; strip health details from prompts
Prepare the AFAS mutation and route it to the administrator
Escalate unclear cases to a ticket with the profile attached
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves each mutation and anything touching sickness or WIA.
data_needed: Letter templates from UWV, pension fund, insurer
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier and workflow log; bot conversation log reviewed with works council.

evidence.claim: An HR agent answers questions per region, contract and tenure and makes a ticket with profile when it cannot.
AFAS Profit 8 Jonas reads documents into dossier fields.
A chatbot alone saves about 3% of hours; gains need workflow redesign.
Health data is special-category and should stay out of model prompts.

risks: Health data leaking into prompts or logs (GDPR Art. 9)
Works council consent required under WOR art. 27(1)(k)
Wrong entitlement quoted if CAO rules are not maintained
research_questions: What are the top 20 benefit questions and their share of volume?
How accurate is Jonas on UWV and pension fund letters at Noordhaven?
Will the OR consent to a bot that answers from the personnel file?

tasks.short: Write and publish vacancies in Recruitee and job boards, and post them internally first as the CAO requires.

today.trigger: Hiring manager approves a vacancy request.
steps: Collect role details from the manager by email
Write or adapt the vacancy text in Recruitee
Post internally on SharePoint/Teams for the internal period
Publish to job boards and inform staffing agencies for flex roles
today.time_sinks: Getting complete details from managers and reformatting texts per channel.

lenses.faster: An intake form feeds an LLM that drafts the vacancy in NL and EN from the role family template with the right CAO scale.
lenses.autonomous: Approval triggers the internal post, a timer for the internal period, then external publication.
lenses.ambitious: Every vacancy is posted internally with matched eligible employees notified personally, raising internal mobility.
lenses.joy: No more chasing managers for the shift pattern; the administrator edits a draft instead of a blank page.
lenses.options: Three versions per vacancy (formal, short mobile, Polish for warehouse) for testing which brings applicants.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns templates and the posting rules, and checks results per channel.
reach: Recruiter: channel choice and vacancy copy

tasks.human_edge: Checking the text is honest about the work and agreeing the profile with the manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured intake to a drafted text inside a fixed publishing workflow; output is checkable.

in_practice.trigger: Vacancy approved in the intake form.
steps: LLM drafts text from template, intake and CAO scale
Administrator edits and approves
Automated internal post and notify eligible employees
After internal period publish externally
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves each text before publication.

evidence.claim: LLMs draft job adverts from structured input.

risks: Notifying employees by profile matching may need OR consent
research_questions: How long is the average vacancy from approval to publication today?
Does internal notification by profile matching need OR consent?
Do variant texts raise applicant numbers?

tasks.short: Answer outside requests about employees: werkgeversverklaringen for mortgages, UWV questions, wage garnishments, reference checks.

today.trigger: Request by email from employee, bank, UWV, bailiff or another employer.
steps: Check the requester is authorised and the employee consented
Search AFAS for salary, contract and dates
Fill the form or letter
Get it signed and send it, then file a copy
drudgery: Copying salary and contract dates into forms
today.time_sinks: Finding the right numbers and checking authorisation.

lenses.faster: The request is classified, the AFAS data pulled and the form filled, so the administrator only checks and signs.
lenses.autonomous: Employees request their own werkgeversverklaring through a form; it is pre-filled from AFAS on arrival.
lenses.ambitious: Mortgage and rent declarations same-day for all staff.
lenses.joy: No more transcription; the administrator focuses on sensitive requests like garnishments.
lenses.options: Not much value here; one correct output is the point.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the authorisation rules and approves.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a requester is entitled to data and handling garnishment conversations.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps and an authorisation check; a person signs before anything leaves.

in_practice.trigger: Request in the HR mailbox or self-service form.
steps: Classify request type and requester
Check consent/legal basis against rules
Pull data from AFAS and fill template
Administrator reviews and signs
Send and log

evidence.claim: AFAS Pocket lets employees submit data themselves; self-service is available.
Form filling from HR data is a deterministic merge.

risks: Data released to an unauthorised party (GDPR breach)
Wrong salary figure on a mortgage declaration
research_questions: What volume per request type per month?
Which requests need explicit employee consent?
Can AFAS generate the standard werkgeversverklaring natively?

tasks.short: Make monthly HR reports: headcount, verzuim, flex workers, turnover, and the yearly works council and CBS numbers.

today.trigger: Month end, OR meeting, or ad hoc request.
steps: Export data from AFAS and agency portals
Clean and combine in Excel
Build tables and charts
Write a short commentary and send
drudgery: Monthly copy-paste of the same exports
Reconciling flex worker hours across three agencies

lenses.faster: Reports come from the nightly Power BI model; the administrator only reviews.
lenses.autonomous: Subscriptions send reports on schedule; an LLM writes a draft commentary on changes.
lenses.ambitious: Each site manager gets a monthly view of verzuim, flex and retention vs. North Star.
lenses.joy: No more Excel rebuilding; the administrator explains numbers instead.
lenses.options: Commentary in different lengths for director, OR and site managers.
lenses.altitude: The administrator defines report rules and checks data quality.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard report maintenance

tasks.human_edge: Explaining what the numbers mean for the OR and managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured data, fixed definitions, checkable output.

steps: Nightly AFAS extract and agency data loaded
Power BI paginated report built
LLM drafts commentary on changes
Administrator reviews and sends

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled report subscriptions and paginated reports.

risks: Small group numbers can identify individuals
research_questions: Which reports are recurring vs ad hoc?
Can agency portals export in a fixed format?
Is the data model trusted by Finance?

tasks.short: Keep the org chart, personeelsgids, phone lists and appraisal forms on SharePoint current.

today.trigger: Org changes, CAO updates, new policy.
steps: Notice a change
Edit Word or Visio files
Get approval
Publish to SharePoint
drudgery: Finding every place a rule appears
today.time_sinks: Keeping documents in sync with AFAS and the CAO.

lenses.faster: The org chart and directories come from AFAS; an LLM proposes handbook edits when a CAO changes.
lenses.autonomous: A new CAO version triggers a diff and a list of handbook sections to update.
lenses.ambitious: A single source used by the HR bot, always current, in NL, EN and PL.
lenses.options: Draft alternative wordings for policy changes for the HR Director.
lenses.altitude: The administrator becomes the knowledge owner of HR content.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing policy wording and getting OR consent.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured parts are generated; policy text needs approval.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS org change or new CAO.
steps: Regenerate org chart and directory from AFAS
LLM drafts handbook changes
Administrator and HR BP approve
Publish
in_practice.human_gate: Approval of all policy text; OR where needed.

evidence.claim: Content structure and named owners matter more than the model for HR bots.
SixFifty drafts handbooks on an expert-maintained law base.

research_questions: How often does the handbook drift from the CAO?
Can AFAS export reporting lines cleanly?
Who owns each section?

role.altitude: From doing HR transactions by hand to owning HR knowledge and rules, and handling the exceptions queue of automated workflows in AFAS, Recruitee and Microsoft 365.
reach: Recruiter: first screens and candidate communication
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: first-line benefit questions
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard reports
role.ceiling_note: Limited by health data, works council consent (WOR art. 27), AI Act high-risk rules on screening from December 2027, and content quality; roughly 40-50% of task hours can return.
skills_to_grow: Workflow and rule design in AFAS and Power Automate
role.ambitious_version: Run an HR service desk where most questions are answered on owned content, every dossier is complete on day one, and the administrator measures and improves resolution without a ticket.
